title: Design a Deduplicated Image Storage Service
prompt:
Design an image service with upload, view, and delete. Uploads can be large and retried; the service must compute a full-file SHA-256, deduplicate identical blobs, preserve separate user-visible image records, and safely garbage-collect an unreferenced blob.

Cover resumable multipart upload, integrity verification, idempotency, metadata/blob consistency, concurrent finalization, authorization, delete races, failure recovery, and observability. Do not assume a multipart ETag is a full-file SHA-256. This is a practice reconstruction of a reported image-storage interview theme.

response.placeholder: Separate an upload session, a verified immutable blob, and a user-visible image reference.
response.reference_answer:
## Data model

An upload session is idempotent by client key and moves through uploading, verifying, ready, failed, and abandoned states. A verified blob is keyed by a full-file SHA-256 plus size and immutable storage location. An image record belongs to a principal and references one blob; it is not the blob itself.

## Upload and deduplication

The client uploads resumable parts to a temporary object while the service tracks part integrity and computes or verifies the complete SHA-256 at finalization. Only after full-object verification does a transaction or compare-and-set register the canonical blob. Concurrent finalizers for the same hash attach to the one blob record. A failure between object upload and metadata commit leaves a recoverable temporary object, not a ready image.

## Read, delete, and recovery

Reads authorize the image record before issuing a short-lived object URL or streaming bytes. Delete tombstones the image reference first, then a background collector removes a blob only when its reference count is zero and no finalization lease is active. Reconciliation scans terminal sessions and object metadata to repair orphaned temporary objects and incomplete transitions.

## Operations

Track upload completion, resume and retry rates, verification failures, deduplication savings, finalization races, orphan age, deletion lag, authorization failures, and storage reclaimed. The source-of-truth state machine makes blob lifetime explainable even if object-store and metadata operations are not one transaction.
